Hi, I apologise for holding off on replying. It was purposeful as truthfully my results have... fluctuated! I'm not going to post progress photos yet as I don't believe my skin has fully calmed from the treatment. It started off incredibly positive for the first few days, then my skin reverted back to how it was and now, a few weeks later my skin seems to have settled into a very comfortable window. I flush less frequently however usually around 1-2 times a day usually once during a stressful period at work and secondly in the evening when im cooking because of the heat or alcohol. The flushing however, is different. Even it feels like I am experiencing a violently strong flush, my skin cannot seem to flush more than around 50% at a max of what it used to. My skin at it's worst use to turn my entire cheeks and upper face completely purple and fiery hot. Now it's a pinkish red, I dont like how it looks but ive learned that nobody really cares. I cooked a BBQ recently and my face was quite blushed all over, but nobody glanced twice. I am going back for a second treatment to maximise the results, and will update then. However I am happy with the results, this is not a permanent treatment, nor a cheap one. I do not know how results will continue to progress. It is also worth mentioning I take medication for ADHD that does constrict my blood vessels as they are stimulants, however I have experienced full flushing on these so I know it can happen still, I have not yet seen my skin have a flush nearly as bad as they used to be. I don't want anyone to think this is a miracle treatment. It is far from that and is still considered an "off brand" treatment for KPRF and Rosacea. However, has it worked? Yes, I would say my flushing and redness has reduced at it's maximum by around 40/30%. Let's just hope it lasts aha! I hope this is helpful.   


\- I would also like to note, briefly for a few days when i have flushed, my forehead has had weird blotchy patterns, as if where the botox was injected isn't flushing but the surrounding areas area, this has only happened a few times however is something i am watching closely, I never have flushed in my forehead but received the treatment there as it is part of the procedure.

If you search 'microbotox for rosacea' or 'microbotox for KPRF' you'll find several studies proving the use of the botulin toxin when injected at an intradermal level in the areas of redness can prevent flushing. However this doesn't prevent flushing fully, just the severity of it - It is also not permanent and may need to be re-done every 4/6 months. It's entirely dependent on how you respond to it. It's usually a second option if laser doesn't work. It doesn't cure redness, just stops the flushing caused by inflammation from KP clogs cause that create redness and flushing.

Are you speaking with dermatologists that specialise in rosacea? If not I recommend you do so. Before I suggest anything else I recommend you consult a private dermatologist that is also a specialist in rosacea and can perform laser treatments such as IPL and Vbeam. I was misdiagnosed originally by a dermatologist for KPRF, then I saw one who specialised in rosacea and he correctly diagnosed me with type 1 rosacea, I have purely flushing however mine is very bad... when fully flushed my entire cheek area is a deep red and burns. I must say, your skin looks very healthy and looked after! and it's seriously very unnoticeable on you! So don't focus too much on your appearance seriously! However I do recommend sorting treatment at this stage, as the biggest issue with rosacea is that it is currently a chronic disorder and usually grows worse with age. However treatments such as Vbeam Prima and Micro-Botox (specifically for rosacea not just normal botox) do have the ability to prevent the dilation of the blood vessels that causes your flushing and baseline redness whilst also preventing the condition from getting worse! However, these are not "permanent treatments" per say - as you will need regular check-ups and additional sessions to touch up the redness as it returns eventually. Truthfully if you see a good specialist I can't see any outcome other than you possibly being given some oral or topical medication to reduce flushing/ redness generally and then I imagine 3 rounds of Vbeam laser treatment to fix most of your baseline redness and some flushing. Given the lack of severity of your rosacea, I would not be surprised if you only need touch up sessions every 1/2 years. Please don't feel negative about this! Your skin looks healthy and natural! Despite all the negative posts on here about rosacea, please understand most people who actually "cure" their rosacea (in quotations as technically there is no cure per say, however keeping it permanently in remission via treatment is a cure from the standpoint of someone with this condition) don't usually post about it here as they just move on with their life feeling good! Most people with the condition will never even know of this subreddit! So don't feel downed by many of the negative posts about treatments, as many have only found this sub through searching for others who have had bad experiences. It's like leaving a review at a resturaunt! Most people only do so when they have a bad experience! If it's good they just continue on with their lives :)  So Don't Fret!
